findings.summary: The no-arg `calls()` total is asserted only where the old and new counting sites agree, so moving `calls++` back into `refuseIfPartitioned` survives all 494 tests and reinstates the exact blindness M5.29 removes -- for the total.
findings.detail: MUTATION MEASURED, SURVIVING: delete `calls++` from `FaultInjectingStore.record` (FaultInjectingStore.java:193) and put it back as the first statement of `refuseIfPartitioned`. `byVerb` and therefore `calls(String)` and `GracefulReleaseMeter` stay correct, so the 1,000-seed sweep is byte-identical (1,608 / 0 / 38 / 12) and the full `:sequencer:test` is 494/494 GREEN. What changes is the no-arg `calls()`: `capabilities`, `close` and `presign` stop being counted in the total -- the three verbs this commit exists to stop missing -- and `list` stops being counted on the ~3% where its injected `unreachable` fires first. INVISIBLE BECAUSE THE ONLY ASSERTION OVER `calls()` IN THE TREE IS THIS ONE: `theMeterNamesTheVERBAndNotMerelyTheCOUNT` asserts `calls()` is 3 over one `put` and two `stat`s, and all three pass through `refuseIfPartitioned`, so the total is 3 under either counting site. `theVerbsThatSKIPThePartitionCheckAreStillCOUNTED` (FaultInjectingStoreTest:92) exercises exactly the three verbs that would diverge and reads only `calls(String)`, never the total. NOT COVERED BY THE M5.49 ROW: its proposed grep -- every `@Override` in this file contains a `record(...)` -- is satisfied, because every `record` call is still present and still at the top of its verb. MINOR, NOT MAJOR: after this commit `calls()` has no consumer outside that one assertion, so nothing regresses today; this is M5.29's own staleness class at a new site, and the row already warns that the next hand makes it real. KILL, ONE LINE: append `assertThat(faulty.calls()).isEqualTo(3)` to `theVerbsThatSKIPThePartitionCheckAreStillCOUNTED` after the `close()` -- it is 0 mutated.
findings.failure_scenario: A later hand tidies `FaultInjectingStore` -- `record` looks like it does two unrelated things, so `calls++` goes back into `refuseIfPartitioned` where it lived until this commit. All 494 tests stay green and the 1,000-seed sweep is identical, so nothing says a word. The next time somebody reaches for the no-arg `calls()` to answer "did this window do store work" -- which is what M5.26 did -- they get a total that silently omits `capabilities`, `close`, `presign` and the ~3% of `list` calls whose injected fault fires first, and a release coming to rest on any of them reds a floor with no defect present. That is M5.29's opening sentence, recreated in a file whose whole subject is preventing it.

findings.summary: M5.35's `writesBefore = 0` cell is faithful in every direction I could measure, except the test count: `all 493 tests` is 494 on this tree, and was 488 before this commit.
findings.detail: RE-MEASURED, ALL THREE CLAIMS HOLD. (1) `int writesBefore = 0` at GracefulReleaseMeter.java:52 survives the whole `:sequencer:test` with the sweep totals unchanged to the digit -- 1,608 graceful releases, 0 refused for another pod, 38 refusals seen, 12 zero-commit seeds, identical to the unmutated baseline I ran on this tree. (2) The production swap alone -- `leases.release()` at LocalSequencer.java:576 replaced by `store.stat(leases.key())` -- drives `gracefulReleases` to 0 and REDS `CommitProtocolSweepTest.theInvariantsHoldAcrossEverySeed` (plus 32 other tests). (3) The same swap PLUS `writesBefore = 0` leaves `CommitProtocolSweepTest` GREEN at 1,385 graceful releases against the floor of `SEEDS` = 1,000. So the compound claim -- that one mutation restores exactly the blindness this task removes -- is correct as written, and the proposed kill (a second `observe` on the same store and meter with an empty lambda, asserting `released()` is 1) would work: mutated, the guard reads `calls("putIfMatch") > 0`, which is true in the second window. THE ONE INACCURACY IS THE COUNT: `:sequencer:test` runs 494 tests with this diff staged and 488 without it, so `all 493 tests` matches neither state. It changes no conclusion -- `survives all tests` is exactly true -- so it is minor, and rule 11 says fixing it buys a round's surface for nothing. Recorded rather than corrected.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever takes M5.35 reads `survives all 493 tests`, runs `:sequencer:test`, sees 494, and cannot tell whether the extra test is one that now kills the mutation or whether the row was written against a different tree. They either re-derive the whole compound measurement to find out, or take the row on trust after the number under it has already been shown wrong once.
